title: Incident Alert
flow: 2 React apps → 4 ASP.NET services ⇄ RabbitMQ + 2 × PostgreSQL
description: Citizens report incidents on a map with photos; nothing reaches the public map until a moderator approves it. Four ASP.NET Core 10 services: a public API, a moderation service with its own database, ML.NET k-means grouping of similar reports, and statistics with hot spots and daily trends. Reports, approvals and categories travel as MassTransit events over RabbitMQ, photos included. Accounts are approved by an admin, and Google ID tokens are verified on the server. 94 backend and 108 frontend tests; CI runs an end-to-end smoke test against the whole Docker stack and publishes the images to GHCR.

title: eMobilityHub
flow: Angular → Nginx → Spring Boot API + 2 JSP apps → MySQL
description: Electric vehicle rental platform made of four apps on one database: an Angular back office for admins, operators and managers, a mobile-first JSP shop where clients rent, pay by card and get a PDF invoice, a JSP promotions portal, and the Spring Boot API. Operators see the fleet on an OpenStreetMap map; managers get revenue and fault statistics.

title: Chat Room
flow: React → Nginx (TLS) → Spring Boot (WAF · SIEM) → MySQL (TLS)
description: Secure internet forum where accounts are approved by an admin and every comment waits for a room moderator. Two-factor sign-in with an emailed code, Google OAuth2, and revocable JWT sessions in an httpOnly cookie. TLS on every hop with certificates from an internal OpenSSL CA; a WAF hit ends the sender's session and a SIEM logs 18 kinds of security events. 219 backend and 86 frontend tests.

title: Online Library System
flow: 7 Java apps ⇄ REST · TCP/TLS · multicast · MQ · RMI + Redis
description: Distributed library platform of seven Java applications: three Swing clients for the library, members and suppliers, plus a REST API, a discovery server, a supplier server that downloads books from Project Gutenberg, and an RMI accounting server. Each link uses the protocol that fits it: REST, TCP and TLS sockets, UDP multicast, RabbitMQ and RMI. Supplier orders go through durable queues, invoices get 17% VAT over RMI, and nothing is Java-deserialized off the wire. 171 tests.

title: RepoHealth
description: A health monitor for all of my public repositories. Each one is checked for a README, a license, tests, CI/CD and recent commits, then scored from 0 to 100, every week.
highlights: Weekly scan of every public repository, with the time of the last scan shown
Totals at a glance: repositories, average score, passing and needing attention
Search plus passing / warning / critical filters; a card with the score per repo
SvelteKit on Vercel, with a strict Content Security Policy

title: FitForge
description: Plan weekly workouts, log sets as you train, and watch strength grow over time.
highlights: Plans per weekday from 230+ exercises, each with its own sets, reps and weight targets
Automatic progression after N good sets in a row (default 8); reps or seconds for bodyweight
Rest timer on the lock screen; charts with estimated 1RM (Epley) and personal records
JSON backup · Riverpod + GoRouter, SQLite · English, Serbian Latin and Cyrillic
imageAlt: FitForge: home, a workout with progression and the rest timer, and progress charts with estimated 1RM

title: Store Chain Management
description: Desktop app for running a retail chain — stores, staff, stock, discounts, shopping and reports — built around a MySQL database that enforces the business rules itself.
highlights: 17 tables, 41 stored procedures, 21 triggers, 5 functions and 11 views
An order is one transaction from a JSON cart, with a full rollback on missing stock
Admin, employee and customer roles; EAN-8, UPC-A, EAN-13 and GTIN-14 barcode checks
76 unit + 101 integration tests on Testcontainers MySQL 8.4 · tagged releases
imageAlt: Store Chain Management: shopping view with products and the cart

title: ETF Oglasi
description: University announcements and class schedules with full offline support — my graduation thesis.
highlights: All boards cached in SQLite; search ignores case, diacritics and Latin/Cyrillic script
Weekly schedules by programme and year, teacher or room; export to calendar (.ics)
New-announcement notifications per board, plus reminders 5–30 min before class
Home screen widgets in native Kotlin · Serbian Latin/Cyrillic + English
imageAlt: ETF Oglasi: categories, announcements and class schedule

title: Store Management
description: Desktop app for running a retail store, with separate administrator and cashier roles.
highlights: Till with bar code scanning; expired or out-of-stock goods refused by the app and the DB
Dashboard: today's sales, stock value, low stock and expiry counts, 14-day sales chart
Sales run as transactional stored procedures with row locks · BCrypt passwords
.NET 10 · 3 languages · 90 unit + 30 Testcontainers integration tests
imageAlt: Store Management: admin dashboard with the sales chart, and the cashier till with a cart

title: AssetManager
description: Android app for tracking company assets — furniture, electronics, office supplies — who has them and where they are.
highlights: Full CRUD, with barcodes typed in or scanned with the camera
OpenStreetMap view: city pins that list the assets at each location
Inventory lists that record changes of employee and location
Riverpod + SQLite · English / Serbian · light and dark theme
imageAlt: AssetManager: home, asset details and workers list in the light theme

title: DevKit
description: 30 developer tools in 7 groups, in one tab. No backend, no tracking, no ads — everything runs in the browser and responds as you type.
highlights: Data: JSON, YAML, Base64, JWT decode & sign, hashes, Protobuf generator
Text & generators: regex, diff, SQL formatter, UUID v4/v7, passwords, TOTP, QR codes
Web & project: HTTP client, URL builder, IP/CIDR calculator, cron parser
Ctrl+K palette with fuzzy search over tools and saved snippets; a #/tool link per tool
Installable offline PWA, one lazy chunk per tool · 19 unit + 7 Playwright e2e tests

title: Catan Map Generator
description: Random, balanced Catan boards generated with constraint-solving backtracking instead of blind retries.
highlights: Standard (19 tiles), Cities & Knights with a barbarian track, Extended 5–6 player (30 tiles)
Places resources, then numbers densest-first; scores up to 8 candidates in ~2.5 s
Share links carry the finished map in the URL hash (21 bytes for a standard board)
Fairness overlay with pips per spot · PNG export · 54 unit + 14 Playwright e2e tests

title: Minimal Blog
description: A small Django blog: write posts in a rich-text editor, keep them as drafts, publish, and moderate visitors' comments. 90 tests at 99% coverage, run on both SQLite and PostgreSQL.
highlights: A draft is a post without a publish date; comments stay hidden until approved
Data-changing actions are POST-only with CSRF tokens; comment text always escaped
Docker Compose with PostgreSQL 16, or SQLite for local development
CI: Ruff, missing-migration check, tests on 2 databases, Docker smoke test
imageAlt: Minimal Blog: a post with approved comments and edit controls

title: Countdown
description: As many timers as you like, to a duration or a date. Remaining time is never stored or decremented: each timer keeps an absolute target and the display is always target − now, so it survives refreshes, sleep and offline periods.
highlights: Repaint loop pauses in hidden tabs and recalculates the moment you return
Share links carry the timer in the URL hash — the same moment in every timezone
Recurring timers with month-end clamping: Jan 31 → Feb 28 → Mar 31
Tags, .ics calendar export with RRULE, JSON backup · 5 synthesised alert sounds
Installable PWA · zero dependencies · 57 unit + 10 Playwright e2e tests

title: Dev Timeline
description: Reads any public GitHub profile and turns language usage and repo topics into a skill timeline — which languages were used, and when.
highlights: Skills map: language and tooling bars plus a language-by-year heatmap
Timeline view: repos grouped by creation year, with tags and links
Default profile loads from a deploy-time snapshot, so no token ever reaches the browser
Contribution calendar for the last year · live scans cached in localStorage for an hour
React 19 + Vite, no UI or state libraries · 25 unit + 5 Playwright e2e tests

title: Brick Breaker
description: Retro arcade game in the style of DX-Ball 2 and Arkanoid, with 100 levels, 30 power-ups and a built-in level editor. A bot has played every built-in level to the end to prove it can be cleared.
highlights: Hand-rolled ball physics with substeps, so the ball never tunnels through bricks
11 kinds of bricks; levels are plain JSON and level sets can be shared
Everything drawn in code; most music and sound effects generated · English / Serbian
190 GUT tests in 18 scripts · builds for the web, Windows and Android

title: Snake (Blavor)
description: Classic Snake for the Windows desktop with a second player, wrap-around walls, rising speed and remappable keys. In demo mode a bot takes the shortest path to the mouse unless that would trap it.
highlights: Rules live in a UI-free core library; WPF only draws, keeps time and handles input
Two snakes move at once: every target cell is worked out before anyone moves
Sound effects synthesised to WAV in memory; maps from 15×15 to 25×25
136 tests, including 5 UI automation tests that drive the real game
imageAlt: Snake: the snake on a 17×23 grid with score, best and speed

title: Arcane Keep
description: Endless tower defense on procedurally generated maps, with waves that scale until they are genuinely dangerous. The whole simulation runs in tile space on a fixed 1/60 s timestep — no DOM, no React, no pixels — so combat is deterministic and seedable.
highlights: 5 towers, 15 evolutions — including an Obelisk support tower that buffs everything in range
9 enemy types; Dread Lord bosses every 5th wave, Void Overlords from wave 20
Daily challenge: same map and waves for everyone, seeded from the date
All audio synthesised with Web Audio · 8 Vitest suites, 106 assertions · plays offline

title: Monte Carlo π · Python
description: One NumPy package that estimates π three ways: in the browser, in a Jupyter notebook and on the command line. The web version runs real Python and NumPy locally through Pyodide, with no server.
highlights: About 45 million points per second on one core, about 28 million in the browser
Blocks instead of loops: close to 200 times faster than the first version
Stops exactly on a decimal match: per-block cumulative sum plus a PCG64 rewind
32 tests · pytest + ruff on Python 3.11 and 3.13 · notebook executed in CI

title: ANOVA
description: One-factor analysis of variance on the desktop. The F-test, the effects and a contrast between any two alternatives update as you type, with critical values from exact inverse CDFs.
highlights: 2–12 alternatives × 2–200 measurements; paste from Excel or open a CSV
Separate confidence levels for the F-test and the contrast (e.g. 97.5%)
SSA computed directly from the effects, not as SST − SSE, to keep precision
37 tests · CI builds a self-contained single-file .exe on every push
imageAlt: ANOVA: measurements table, F-test result and the effects of each alternative

title: Monte Carlo π
description: Estimates π by throwing random points at a square and shows them land live, turning correct digits green. Runs at about a billion points per second on 12 cores.
highlights: Own xoshiro256** generator with SplitMix64 streams: reproducible however work is split
Parallel.For over chunks of 2²⁰ points; a WriteableBitmap keeps millions on screen
Convergence chart with the theoretical 95% band
28 tests · "until decimals match" mode with reproducible seeds
imageAlt: Monte Carlo π: millions of points in the circle, the estimate and the convergence chart

title: Echo Player
description: Adds a feedback echo to WAV recordings, with a live preview while you shape it and every repeat drawn in the waveform. Preview and output share one NAudio provider, so what you hear is exactly what gets saved.
highlights: Delay 20–2000 ms, feedback 0–90%, mix; 5 presets from Slapback to Canyon
The whole tail is kept until the repeats fade to −60 dB (at most 30 s)
Batch processing in parallel, with progress and cancellation; bit depth preserved
36 tests · the core has no audio-hardware dependency
imageAlt: Echo Player: original and echoed waveforms with the echo controls

title: Secure Repository
description: A document vault on a private OpenSSL certificate authority. Every document gets its own key, is signed, split into parts, and each part is encrypted and signed on its own, so a tampered part is named before anything is decrypted.
highlights: Private CA (4096-bit RSA); X.509 user certificates valid 180 days, revoked through a CRL
Per-document AES-256 key wrapped with RSA-OAEP; 4–9 parts, each encrypted then signed
Two-factor sign-in: password (PBKDF2, 600,000 iterations) plus certificate
144 tests, including integration tests against real OpenSSL · CI on Windows and Linux
imageAlt: Secure Repository: signing in with a certificate and downloading a verified document

title: e-Mobility Rental
description: Multithreaded simulation of an electric car, bike and scooter rental company. Every rental runs in its own thread on a shared 20×20 city map, for exactly as many seconds as it lasts.
highlights: Rentals in a time slot run in parallel and are joined before the next slot starts
Invoices per ride, daily and summary reports, a binary file per vehicle
Nothing hard-coded: prices, map size and formats in app.properties; BigDecimal money
123 JUnit 5 tests, including a headless simulation run · CI builds the JAR and Javadoc
imageAlt: e-Mobility Rental: vehicles moving across the city map, with active rentals and invoices

title: GitHub Discord Bot
description: A bot that bridges GitHub and Discord for solo work: manage issues, track activity and get reports without leaving chat.
highlights: Open issues with /add or a form, close them with one click; labels detected from the title
HMAC-signed webhook posts issues, PRs, failed CI runs and releases to Discord
Monthly report on the 1st and a Monday reminder of stale issues
discord.py + Flask · Supabase PostgreSQL · Render, deployed after CI · 232 tests, 99% coverage

title: GitHub Dashboard
description: Terminal-style analytics for any GitHub user, with no backend and no token in the browser. The default profile ships as a JSON snapshot built at deploy time; any other username loads live.
highlights: Profile, top languages, repositories by year and a GitHub-style contribution heatmap
Pinned repos first, the rest ranked by stars, forks and description; a "vs" comparison
Paginated REST fetches, with a CORS proxy fallback when requests are blocked
Exports to HTML, PNG or PDF · 19 unit + 10 Playwright e2e tests with the API mocked

title: Yamb Table
description: Multiplayer scoresheet for Yamb, Yahtzee and Yatzy with a retro CRT look. Pass the phone around: each player fills in their own sheet while the others can peek, read-only.
highlights: Yamb's four columns with fill-order rules: down, up, free and announce
Mode-specific scoring: upper bonus, straights, full house, poker, Yamb bonus
Dice roller with up to eight ranked suggestions, filled in with one click
2–12 players · undo up to 10 moves, even after a reload
Installable offline PWA · 21 unit + 5 Playwright e2e tests

title: Sedmica
description: Digital scorecard for the card game Sedmica, for 2–4 players — the first player whose total reaches the limit (51 by default) loses.
highlights: Validates every round live: the points must add up to 8 or 9
Šuster rule: mark a round's loser to reset their total to 0 · undo the last round
History of the last 50 games with losses and average total per player
Offline PWA · vanilla JS · 31 unit + 8 Playwright e2e tests

title: Lora Score Table
description: Scorecard for Lora, a four-player card game played across seven contracts — lowest score wins.
highlights: All seven games, from Plus and Minus to Dame, K srca and Lora
Round totals checked (e.g. must add up to 8), with house rules per game
Winner after all 28 rounds; share the result or save the final table as a PNG
Offline PWA · vanilla JS · 27 unit + 6 Playwright e2e tests

title: excuse.exe
description: One button, one excuse — from 1,600+ in English and 1,250+ in Serbian, with no repeats until the whole list has been used.
highlights: Seven categories as filter chips, from Work and Tech to Absurd; an excuse of the day
Every excuse has its own link (#en-0042); favourites saved per language
Offline PWA: network-first pages, cached files refreshed in the background
Zero dependencies, self-hosted fonts · 27 unit + 12 Playwright e2e tests
